# T-002 (M1): CPU and memory collector

Allowed: wsd/collectors/__init__.py wsd/collectors/system.py wsd/routes.py wsd/__main__.py tests/test_system.py tests/fixtures/system/*

Do not change wsd/server.py.

wsd/collectors/system.py (stdlib only; every reader takes a `root` path argument defaulting to "/", so tests can point at fixtures):
- `parse_proc_stat(text) -> dict[str, tuple[int, int]]`: per CPU line ("cpu", "cpu0", ...) -> (busy_jiffies, total_jiffies). Busy = total - idle - iowait.
- `cpu_utilisation(prev, cur) -> dict[str, float | None]`: percent busy per CPU between two parse results, rounded to 1 dp. Return None for a CPU whose total did not increase.
- `read_cpu_freqs_mhz(root) -> list[float | None]`: from sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu<N>/cpufreq/scaling_cur_freq (kHz), sorted by N. None where the file is missing.
- `parse_meminfo(text) -> dict`: total, available, used (= total - available), swap_total, swap_used, all in bytes.
- `class CpuSampler(root)`: `sample()` returns {"overall": %, "per_cpu": [%...], "freq_mhz": {"min", "max", "avg", "per_cpu": [...]}}. The first call after construction compares against a reading taken at construction time.
- `read_system(root, sampler) -> dict`: {"cpu": sampler.sample(), "memory": parse_meminfo(...), "load_avg": [1m, 5m, 15m] from proc/loadavg, "uptime_s"}. A missing file gives None for that part, not an exception.

wsd/routes.py: registers `/api/system` with `server.route`, using one module-level CpuSampler. wsd/__main__.py: `import wsd.routes` before starting the server.

tests/test_system.py with small fixture files under tests/fixtures/system/ (copy the format from this machine's real /proc files, but trim them to 2–4 CPUs): parser values, utilisation maths (including the no-change case), missing cpufreq -> None, missing meminfo -> memory None, and /api/system returning 200 with the expected keys.

Acceptance: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -q` passes; all T-001 tests still pass.
